Subject: Recap: private deployment performance acceptance & next steps

Hi Ben / Lumina infra team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good visibility into your expected inference patterns. Below is a concise acceptance-scope and proposed next steps so we can align test criteria for your private VPC deployment. If anything below is off, flag it and we'll adjust.

Performance acceptance targets (proposed):
- Latency (inference only, single-request): p50 <= 30ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 250ms (measured from Redwood edge within your VPC to model response; excludes client-side processing)
- Throughput: steady-state 600 tokens/sec (aggregate for the model pool), burst up to 1,800 tokens/sec for 90s windows
- Concurrency: sustained 40 concurrent inference sessions, burst concurrency up to 140 for autoscaling validation
- Streaming: support chunked token streaming with max chunk size 512 tokens and inter-chunk latency <= 50ms

Network / deployment constraints to validate:
- Private peering or VPN: route must support 10 Gbps baseline with 20 Gbps headroom for burst tests
- Egress: no middlebox inspection that rewrites TLS or truncates long-lived streaming sockets
- Internal latency budget: cross-subnet hop budget <= 5ms within the VPC (for GPU fleet access)

Acceptance test artifacts we will provide:
- redwood-acceptance-template.xlsx (test matrix + SLA pass/fail criteria) [attached]
- network-troubleshooting-checklist.pdf (packet capture guidance & endpoints) [attached]
- loadtest script and instructions (we will push a runner and a short plan)

Action items / owners (first pass):
- Lumina: confirm peak sustained token/sec and expected client-side request envelope (Ben) — due 2027-11-18
- Redwood: provide tuned loadtest script, required temporary test credentials, and a DocuSign SLA addendum (Aditya) — due 2027-11-19
- Redwood Infra: review Lumina network topology and call out any peering tweaks (Grace) — due 2027-11-19
- Joint: schedule a 2-hour test window week of Nov 29 for a joint run (Ben + Grace + Vivek) — target scheduling by 2027-11-20

Notes / assumptions:
- Measurements in acceptance are taken from our collector inside your VPC (private control plane) to the serving cluster; final prod SLOs can be tuned post-rollout but acceptance must meet the above.
- If encrypted inspection or TLS termination is present on your side, streaming semantics may degrade; please confirm.

I'll wait for your confirmations and any topology files you can share.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.example.com

Aditya — thanks for the clear writeup. Couple quick clarifications from our side: we can confirm the following tentative numbers today:
- Client envelope: each request ~ 256 tokens average, peak requests will often be bursty for short windows (no more than 90s)
- Expected steady-state tokens/sec: ~550 (close to your 600), bursts to 1,600 are realistic
- Concurrency: steady 35, burst 120 (we budgeted conservatively)

Questions:
1) On streaming: when you say \"max chunk size 512 tokens\" — is that a hard limit for the streaming encoder, or more of a best-practice? Our client-side will hold open HTTP/2 streaming connections for up to 2 minutes.
2) For VPN/peering: attaching our current topology (lumina-network-topology-v2.drawio) — do you expect any obvious bandwidth chokepoints?

We'll attach the topology file and loop in our infra PM if we need a deep dive. Also, we can meet the Nov 29 week for testing — we'll pencil in 2 hours and confirm exact slot after we get the test credentials.

Best,

Thanks Ben — quick answers and an initial test plan.

Streaming behavior:
- The 512-token chunk is a recommended upper bound to keep per-chunk serialization and network RTTs low. It's not a hard protocol limit; if you stream larger chunks we will still deliver, but inter-chunk latency may increase.
- Redwood's streaming path keeps a persistent HTTP/2 connection; backpressure is managed via small chunks and pacing. 2-minute client-held streams are supported, provided there's no intermediate proxy that times out idle streams.

Network observations from attached topology (quick scan):
- The topology looks fine at a glance. Watch for the transit VPC peering through the legacy NAT gateway in us-west-2 — that gateway currently caps at ~10 Gbps if not migrated to NGW autoscaling; recommend you validate that path for burst windows.
- Recommend reserving a dedicated peering link or ensuring the VPN has 20 Gbps headroom during the test window.

Proposed quick test plan (we'll provide scripts):
1) Baseline connectivity check (10x small requests, verify p50/p95)
2) Incremental concurrency ramp (steps: 10 -> 25 -> 40 -> 80 -> 120) with 5-minute steady periods
3) Burst stress (3x 90s bursts at target burst tokens/sec)
4) Streaming validation (open 50 concurrent streaming connections, measure inter-chunk latency and socket stability)

Attachments we are uploading to the shared folder: loadtest-script.sh (bash script), and recommended collector endpoints. We'll also create a small Slack channel for live troubleshooting during the run.

Action: Aditya will send temporary test credentials and DocuSign SLA addendum; Vivek and I will review the topology and propose any minor route changes by EOD 11/19.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Principal Infra Solutions | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com
